title: Recurrent Neural Networks for Multivariate Time Series with Missing Values (GRU-D)
methods: Read arXiv version text (pdftotext) for dataset/experiment sections.
findings: PhysioNet 2012 Training Set A used because outcomes public only for this subset; 4,000 records, 33 variables, ~48 h, mean 68.91 time steps, mean variable missing rate 0.8225.
MIMIC-III: 19,714 admissions, 99 features, first 48 h, mean 35.89 time steps, missing rate 0.9621; tasks mortality and 20 ICD-9 categories.
Early prediction with 12-48 h; subsampled 2k/10k admissions for scalability; no demographic subgroup analysis.
limitations: Section numbers follow the arXiv preprint; published in Scientific Reports 8:6085 (2018).

title: BRITS: Bidirectional Recurrent Imputation for Time Series
findings: Health-care data: PhysioNet 2012, 4,000 series, 35 measurements, first 48 h after ICU admission, up to 78% missing; imputation (10% of observed values held out) and in-hospital death (~10% positive).
Air quality series of 36 consecutive steps; human activity localization data.

title: Multi-Time Attention Networks for Irregularly Sampled Time Series (mTAND)
findings: PhysioNet 2012: 37 variables, first 48 h, times rounded to minute -> 2,880 possible times; 8,000 instances (4,000 labeled), 13.8% positive.
MIMIC-III: 53,211 records, 12 physiological variables, first 48 h, 8.1% positive.
Interpolation conditioned on 50-90% observed points; 80/20 random split.

title: Graph-Guided Network for Irregularly Sampled Multivariate Time Series (Raindrop)

locators.main: §4; §4.1; Table 2; Table 3; Appendix A.5; Appendix A.13; Table 6

findings: P19 38,803 patients, 34 sensors, <=60 observations, sepsis within 6 h (~4% positive); P12 11,988 patients, 36 sensors, first 48 h, 215 timestamps, label ICU LOS >3 days (~93% positive); PAM 5,333 segments.
Missing ratio P19 94.9%, P12 88.4%, PAM 60.0% (Table 3).
Settings 2-3 leave 10-50% sensors out; Setting 4 group-wise: train young (<65) test old (>=65) and reverse, male<->female on P19; cross-group AUROC roughly 75-85 across models (Table 6).

title: Set Functions for Time Series (SeFT)
findings: M3-Mortality: Harutyunyan et al. MIMIC-III benchmark subset, first 48 h of ICU stay, ~21,000 stays, ~10% death.
P-Mortality: PhysioNet 2012, 12,000 stays (8,000 train / 4,000 test), ~14% prevalence; excessively long series excluded.
P-Sepsis: PhysioNet 2019, >60,000 ICU patients, hourly, online prediction of sepsis onset 6-12 h ahead.

title: Time Series as Images: Vision Transformer for Irregularly Sampled Time Series (ViTST)
methods: WebFetch of arXiv HTML v2 (first 100k chars).
findings: P19 average 401 observations, P12 average 233 observations (Table 1); data processed as in Raindrop.
Leave-fixed/random-sensors-out on PAM; Swin Transformer pre-trained on ImageNet-21K.
No demographic subgroup analysis reported.
limitations: Last ~2k characters of HTML not read.

title: Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting: A Transformable Patching Graph Neural Networks Approach (t-PatchGNN)
findings: PhysioNet 12,000 IMTS, 41 variables, first 48 h; observe first 24 h, forecast next 24 h.
MIMIC 23,457 patients, 96 variables, first 48 h; same 24 h -> 24 h.
Random 60/20/20 split; Appendix A.1 varies observation/forecast horizons (12/3 h vs 36/45 h).

title: IMTS is Worth Time x Channel Patches: Visual Masked Autoencoders for Irregular Multivariate Time Series Prediction (VIMTS)
methods: WebFetch of arXiv HTML v1 (first 100k chars).
findings: Datasets: PhysioNet 12,000/41 vars/85.7% missing; Human Activity; USHCN; MIMIC 23,457/96 vars/96.7% missing; 24 h observe -> next 24 h for clinical sets; 60/20/20 split.
Task is forecasting; few-shot with 10/20/50% of training data; backbone visual MAE-base.
limitations: Authors list truncated (et al.); last ~10k characters not read.

title: MIRA: Medical Time Series Foundation Model for Real-World Health Data
methods: WebFetch of arXiv HTML v7 (first 100k of 124k chars).
findings: Pretrained on >454 billion time points from public medical data incl. MIMIC-III, MIMIC-IV, PTB-XL, Sleep-EDF, WAVES; max sequence length 512.
Evaluation is forecasting (RMSE/MAE); OOD sets include CinC 2012, Heart Rate, MIT-BIH, CDC-IHA, JH COVID-19, ILI; missing-rate sweep 10-90% on WHO FluNet (Table 4).
No emergency department data named.
limitations: Text says seven OOD benchmarks but Table 2 lists six; appendix (per-dataset details) not read; author list truncated.

title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting (TimesFM)
findings: Pretraining: Google Trends, Wiki pageviews, synthetic, M4, electricity, traffic, weather, Favorita, LibCity; max context 512 (256 weekly, 64 monthly); input patch 32, output patch 128.
Zero-shot Monash, Darts, ETT; no dataset described as clinical.
limitations: 'TimesFM 3.0' used by the collaborator not verified; TimesFM 2.5 (2025-09, 16k context) seen only on third-party pages.

title: Learning Dynamic Representations and Policies from Multimodal Clinical Time-Series with Informative Missingness (OPL-MT-MNAR)
methods: WebFetch of arXiv HTML v1 (first 100k of 213k chars).
findings: Sepsis cohorts following Komorowski 2018: MIMIC-III 15,415, MIMIC-IV 32,837, eICU 24,562 ICU stays; first 72 h at 4 h steps (H=18).
Post-72 h in-hospital mortality AUROC 0.886 on MIMIC-III.
Subgroups: low vs high SOFA (§4.2); within-eICU center-held-out (App B.5); cross-dataset (B.4); heart-failure cohort (B.6); chronological split (M.2).
limitations: Findings of ACL 2026; appendix content not read.

title: Benchmarking emergency department prediction models with machine learning and public electronic health records

locators.main: Benchmark tasks; Methods data processing; Tables 1, 4-6

methods: WebFetch of PMC full text (first 100k chars).
findings: 441,437 adult ED episodes from MIMIC-IV-ED; outcomes: hospitalization, critical outcome (inpatient mortality or ICU transfer within 12 h), 72 h reattendance.
Predictors at triage for hospitalization/critical outcome; random 80/20 split; critical outcome AUROC 0.613 (MEWS) to 0.883 (MLP), gradient boosting 0.880.
No subgroup performance analysis.
limitations: Text does not state when the 12 h window starts or whether the split is grouped by patient.

title: Multimodal Clinical Benchmark for Emergency Care (MC-BEC): A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models in Emergency Medicine
methods: Read NeurIPS 2023 D&B PDF text (task and bias sections).
findings: 102,731 monitored ED visits; decompensation: first 15 min after rooming, predict new HR>110, MAP<65 or SpO2<90 within 60/90/120 min in patients with initially normal vitals (abnormal at triage or assessment excluded).
Disposition and 3/7/14-day revisit tasks.
Bias: TPR difference between age, gender, race, ethnicity groups at validation sensitivity 0.85 (Table 5).
limitations: Authors not recorded in this pass; exact title taken from search result.

title: Multimodal Clinical Monitoring in the Emergency Department (MC-MED) v1.0.1 — PhysioNet project page
findings: 118,385 adult visits to monitored beds of the Stanford adult ED, Sep 2020 - Sep 2022.
Numerics recorded continuously and reported as 1-minute means (HR, RR, SpO2, SBP, DBP, MAP, Temp, ...).
v1.0.1 release note: a small number of de-identified MRNs were re-generated.
notes: Author surnames as listed in search result; full names not checked on the page.
